title: North America capitals five of five · The Windwards and Trinidad
edition: North America capitals · Five regional lessons · John · November 2026
intro: Welcome to the North America capitals, episode five of five. First, I clear the chosen names for a fresh regional lesson.
And four close the series: the Windward islands and Barbados, and the great island of Trinidad at their foot.

states.name: Saint George's
lines: Saint George's stands on the Carenage, a horseshoe harbour, on the west coast of Grenada, with the houses climbing the hills around it.
The French founded it in 1650, and American troops landed here in 1983.
Remember Saint George's as the horseshoe harbour, founded by the French and landed on by Americans in 1983.
states.transition: Let's bring Saint George's into view.

states.name: Kingstown
lines: Kingstown stands on the windward shore of Saint Vincent, below the green slopes of the central mountains.
Its botanic garden, of 1765, is the oldest in the Americas, and Captain Bligh brought breadfruit trees to it. It is called the city of arches, for its stone arcades.
Remember Kingstown as the city of arches, with the oldest botanic garden in the Americas.

states.name: Bridgetown
lines: Bridgetown stands on Carlisle Bay in the west of Barbados, an island of coral limestone in the Atlantic.

Its old town and British garrison are a UNESCO site, and its Parliament, meeting since 1639, is one of the oldest in the Commonwealth. George Washington stayed here in 1751, on the only journey he ever made abroad.
Remember Bridgetown as the Parliament that has met since 1639, and the only country George Washington ever visited abroad.

states.name: Port-of-Spain
lines: Port-of-Spain stands on the Gulf of Paria, on the north-west coast of Trinidad, facing Venezuela across the water.
Its carnival is the largest in the Caribbean, and its Queen's Park Savannah is often called one of the largest roundabouts in the world.
Remember Port-of-Spain as the carnival capital, with a savannah that counts as a roundabout.

recap: Saint George's and Kingstown stand on the Grenadines and Saint Vincent, Bridgetown on the Atlantic side of Barbados, and Port-of-Spain on the Gulf of Paria.
Remember the horseshoe harbour, the city of arches with the oldest botanic garden in the Americas, the Parliament that has met since 1639, and the carnival capital with a savannah roundabout.
